title: Continue, Adapt, or Yield: In-Turn Adaptation to Overlapping Speech in Full-Duplex Agents
one_sentence: Duplex Cue distinguishes content uptake while speaking from unchanged continuation and yielding.
problem: How can evaluation detect responding to an overlapping contribution without stopping?
method: 300 cues from English conversations; recorded responses versus one PersonaPlex generation per cue; 208 pairs active and scorable in both conditions.
findings: Among 66 collaborative pairs, adaptation was 68.2% for recorded speakers and 34.8% for PersonaPlex.
Cue classification used subsequent source behavior, partly building adaptation into the human comparison.
real_contribution: A local uptake category missing from binary floor-retention scoring.
biggest_weakness: Outcome leakage, asymmetric exclusions, bounded converted model history, one model and non-independent adjudication.
claim_boundary: Adaptation includes acknowledgment; it does not establish correct repair, causal cue effects or restored grounding.
why_researcher_should_care: Add uptake as a separate repair-stage measure, then test correct revision and later reuse.
evidence_notes: Full HTML and independent quantitative audit.
Blind cue labeling and no-cue controls are proposed next checks, not completed evidence.

program_membership.reason: Relevant expression, pragmatics, grounding, adaptation, evaluation or system evidence
